name: Question 3
problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $x=\sqrt{2}.$ Given that the point $P(\sqrt{2},2,\frac{1}{2})$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{y}=-\frac{2{x}^{2}+y}{{y}^{3}}$, find the equations of the tangent line to $C$ at $P.$
worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $x=\sqrt{2}.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $P(\sqrt{2},2,\frac{1}{2})$ will be given by the partial derivative $\frac{∂z}{∂y}{|}_{(\sqrt{2},2)}.$

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative $\frac{∂z}{∂y}$ at $(\sqrt{2},2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(\sqrt{2},2) & =-\frac{2(\sqrt{2})^{2}+2}{{2}^{3}} \\  & =-\frac{4+2}{8} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-z{|}_{(\sqrt{2},2)} & =\frac{∂z}{∂y}{|}_{(\sqrt{2},2)}(y-2) \\ z-\frac{1}{2} & =-\frac{3}{4}(y-2) \\ z & =-\frac{3}{4}y+2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(\sqrt{2},2,\frac{1}{2})$ can be given as the intersection of two planes, as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=\sqrt{2} \\ z=-\frac{3}{4}y+2\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

The curve C is the intersection of a surface S, defined by z=f(x,y), with the plane x=2. Given that the point P(2,2,12) lies on C, and that fy=−2x2+yy3, find the equations of the tangent line to C at P.

a
{x=2z=−14y−2
b
{x=2z=12y+2
c
{x=2z=−34y+2
d
{x=2z=32y−1
e
{x=2z=−32y+1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The curve C is the intersection of the surface z=f(x,y) with the plane x=2. Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point P(2,2,12) will be given by the partial derivative ∂z∂y|(2,2).

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ∂z∂y at (2,2):

fy(2,2)=−2(2)2+223=−4+28=−34

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

z−z|(2,2)=∂z∂y|(2,2)(y−2)z−12=−34(y−2)z=−34y+2

Finally, the tangent line to the curve C at P(2,2,12) can be given as the intersection of two planes, as follows: {x=2z=−34y+2
